sample_unit: scripted conversations (100 real people with MS plus 529 simulated derivatives)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT when age, sex, and race/ethnicity were varied in scripted MS conversations
links.effect: After MRI data were included, odds of accurate diagnosis were 4.0-fold greater for Gen Z (p=0.01). Accuracy was 68% lower in males (p=0.009) and 75% lower for White subjects than for non-White subjects (p=0.0004).
links.quote: Post-MRI data inclusion within GPT-3.5, the odds of an accurate diagnosis was 4.0-fold greater for Gen Z participants, relative to non-Gen Z participants (p=0.01) with the diagnostic accuracy being 68% less in males relative to females (p=0.009), and 75% less for White subjects, relative to non-White subjects (p=0.0004).

screen.reason: Retrospective simulation of patient diagnostic journeys using GPT-3.5 compared to clinical timelines, evaluating diagnostic accuracy and demographic bias without testing specific deployment safeguards.
